## {#slide-1 background-color="#0a0a0a"}

::: {.center-v}
### We're Zac & Pete — Development Seed

This is what we're seeing from inside the work.
:::

::: {.notes}
Zac. Quick hello: we're Zac and Pete from Development Seed. Last year, Pete shared an idea about where coding was headed.
:::

## {#slide-2 background-color="#0a0a0a"}

::: {.center-v}
### Last year, Pete predicted more people would create software.
:::

::: {.notes}
Pete. AI would let more people manifest their ideas in code—not just people with “software engineer” in their title.
:::

## {#slide-3 background-color="#0a0a0a"}

::: {.center-v}
### This year, their projects are arriving at our door.
:::

::: {.notes}
Pete. That prediction is already coming true. We're meeting people who didn't wait for a software team to start building.
:::

## {#slide-4 background-color="#0a0a0a"}

::: {.center-v}
![](images/problem.svg){fig-alt="Stick figure surrounded by question marks" width=280}

### And they work.
:::

::: {.notes}
Pete. These aren't imaginary demos. People have built useful things, tested an idea, and found users.
:::

## {#slide-5 background-color="#0a0a0a"}

::: {.center-v}
### Until they need to survive.
:::

::: {.notes}
Pete. Then the project needs another developer, real users, security, operations, or a life beyond the original prompt.
:::

## {#slide-6 background-color="#0a0a0a"}

::: {.center-v}
### AI reduced the cost of starting.

[Not the cost of understanding.]{.green}
:::

::: {.notes}
Pete. Implementation got cheaper. The work around it didn't disappear; it became easier to see.
:::

## {#slide-7 background-color="#0a0a0a"}

::: {.center-v}
![](images/human-network.svg){fig-alt="A dense network of interconnected people with several relationships highlighted" width=1050}

### Clarity lives in relationships.
:::

::: {.notes}
Zac. A model can hold a lot of context. It cannot own the nuance between users, partners, organizations, and the people doing the work.
:::

## {#slide-8 background-color="#0a0a0a"}

::: {.center-v}
### Before: what is actually worth building?
:::

::: {.notes}
Zac. Before implementation, our job is to understand the real problem—not merely turn the first request into code.
:::

## {#slide-9 background-color="#0a0a0a"}

::: {.center-v}
### During: agree on how AI participates.
:::

::: {.notes}
Zac. Treat the agent like a collaborator. Set ground rules for what it generates, what people review, and how decisions get recorded.
:::

## {#slide-10 background-color="#0a0a0a"}

::: {.center-v}
![](images/test.svg){fig-alt="Checklist icon" width=260}

### Tests are part of the prompt.
:::

::: {.notes}
Zac. Tests aren't cleanup after generation. They're part of defining what correct means from the beginning.
:::

## {#slide-11 background-color="#0a0a0a"}

::: {.center-v}
### CI/CD · linting · security scanning

[Guardrails, not garnish.]{.green}
:::

::: {.notes}
Zac. The usual engineering practices matter more when code can arrive faster than people can understand it.
:::

## {#slide-12 background-color="#0a0a0a"}

::: {.center-v}
### Small iterations keep the work understandable.
:::

::: {.notes}
Zac. Small pull requests and short feedback loops let a team maintain shared ownership instead of receiving a wall of generated code.
:::

## {#slide-13 background-color="#0a0a0a"}

::: {.center-v}
### After: following through, validating, recentering?
:::

::: {.notes}
Zac. Productionizing isn't just finishing a repository. Someone has to validate the result and take responsibility for what happens next.
:::

## {#slide-14 background-color="#0a0a0a"}

::: {.center-v}
[APPROVED]{.stamp}

Not a prompt. A relationship.
:::

::: {.notes}
Zac. This is the value we keep returning to: judgment, trust, and the willingness to put our name on the result.
:::

## {#slide-15 background-color="#0a0a0a"}

::: {.center-v}
### Writing code is becoming a smaller part of coding.
:::

::: {.notes}
Pete. Code still matters. But producing lines of it is becoming a smaller share of the complete job.
:::

## {#slide-16 background-color="#0a0a0a"}

::: {.center-v}
### The practitioner's job is becoming larger.
:::

::: {.notes}
Pete. We review, hold context, make design calls, understand risk, talk to users, and maintain the system after the exciting part.
:::

## {#slide-17 background-color="#0a0a0a"}

::: {.center-v}
### More creators. More need for practitioners.
:::

::: {.notes}
Pete. Vibe-coded projects are not failures. They are unfinished successes—and they create more demand for people who know how to help them endure.
:::

## {#slide-18 background-color="#0a0a0a"}

::: {.center-v}
### What we still don't know

How do we price trust, not hours?

How does this stewardship scale?

If AI skips the beginner work, how do beginners become experienced?
:::

::: {.notes}
Pete. These are real open questions. The talent pipeline worries me most: where will tomorrow's experienced practitioners come from?
:::

## {#slide-19 background-color="#0a0a0a"}

::: {.center-v}
### Our wildest hope

More people get to create.

More kinds of expertise shape software.

We make things worth maintaining—not more slop.
:::

::: {.notes}
Pete. The hopeful version is wider participation, more human creativity, and more time spent making the right things well.
:::

## {#slide-20 background-color="#0a0a0a"}

::: {.center-v}
### AI makes it easier to create software.

Our work is helping it become something people can trust.

[Come find us.]{.green}
:::

::: {.notes}
Both. That's what we've been living. Come tell us what you're seeing. Thank you.
:::

## {#slide-applause background-color="#0a0a0a"}

:::

```{=html}
<script>
document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () {
  // Give the title slide a clean URL hash (#/slide-title instead of #/title-slide)
  var ts = document.getElementById('title-slide');
  if (ts) ts.id = 'slide-title';

  // Countdown bar: sits above the RevealJS progress bar, runs right-to-left per slide
  var cdBar = document.createElement('div');
  cdBar.id = 'slide-countdown';
  cdBar.innerHTML = '<div id="slide-countdown-fill"></div>';
  document.querySelector('.reveal').appendChild(cdBar);

  function resetCountdown() {
    var fill = document.getElementById('slide-countdown-fill');
    fill.style.animation = 'none';
    fill.offsetHeight; // force reflow
    fill.style.animation = '';
  }

  Reveal.on('slidechanged', resetCountdown);
  Reveal.on('ready', resetCountdown);
});
</script>
```
